answer_1.quote: Motivated by this, in this paper, we propose a novel approach for conditional generation of rap verses, where the generator is provided a source text and tasked with transferring the style of the text into rap lyrics.

answer_2.quote: We conduct an automatic evaluation of RAP-FORMER, using the test sets of each of our three datasets. Our focus is on measuring two components that are important for generating fluent conditional rap verses: preserving content from the input text to the output, and maintaining rhyming fluency during generation. Content preservation. We test the capacity of our models to preserve content words from the input by computing a unigram overlap score: between unique unigrams from an input text x and the generated output rap verse y. We also report the BLEU score when training a model to reconstruct original lyrics. Rhyming fluency. We measure the technical quality of our rap verses using the rhyme density (RD) metric.

answer_4.quote: Due to the limitations of automatic metrics for text generation, we also perform four human evaluation experiments using three raters, who are trained to translate lyrics.
answer_4.guideline: Questions: 1. How much do the lyrics presented resemble rap lyrics? (1-5 scale). 2. How well do the lyrics preserve the content of the original news article? (1-5 scale). 3. Do these lyrics look like a song you know? (yes/no).
